moat_against: Persistent net outflows ($56.9B in 2025; $6.5B in Q2 2026; reported $28.3B in Q3 2026), concentrated in active equity
Structural shift to passive/index undercuts the core product; no network effect
Fee-rate compression from mix shift to lower-fee vehicles (38.1 bps and falling)
Rising technology and distribution costs squeezing margins
Revenue is a percentage of market levels — a bear market cuts OE mechanically
moat_for: $1.89T AUM scale and 85+ year brand in US retirement channels
Sticky target-date / defined-contribution franchise — retirement assets roughly two-thirds of AUM
Debt-free, cash-rich balance sheet funds buybacks (-1.01%/yr share count) through drawdowns
ETF/SMA and alternatives build-out plus Goldman Sachs partnership gaining flows
moat_justification: Scale, brand, and a sticky retirement/target-date franchise (roughly two-thirds of AUM) are real, but the core fundamental active-equity product is in structural outflow against passive, the effective fee rate is compressing (38.1 bps in Q2 2026 vs 39.6 bps a year earlier), and revenue is a percentage of market levels with no pricing power to offset a drawdown — moderate/narrow moat.
name: T. Rowe Price Group, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality, debt-free retirement-franchise asset manager, moat 5/10 — but structural outflows and fee compression mean it does not clear 15% at $101.49 (weighted IRR 10.4%, IV@15% $63.40); it clears the hurdle only at or below ~$63.40.
